title: New Global Trade Arrangement Gains Momentum – And It’s Worth Watching
gist: A short excerpt flagging the Future of Trade and Investment Partnership (FIT-P), launched September 2025 by Singapore, Switzerland, New Zealand and the UAE, which has grown from 14 to 19 members in ten months and now represents close to 20% of global goods trade. Its Auckland ministerial drew 21 countries and it is framed as a diversification instrument focused on supply chains, non-tariff barriers and technology integration rather than a move away from the U.S., China or EU.

insights.claim: The Future of Trade and Investment Partnership (FIT-P) was launched in September 2025 by four trade-dependent countries — Singapore, Switzerland, New Zealand and the United Arab Emirates — and debuted with 14 members including Chile, Morocco, Norway, Uruguay, Rwanda and Brunei.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Identifies a small-open-economy trade bloc forming outside the WTO and the U.S.-China axis that most macro coverage has not priced or tracked.
insights.locator: Launched in September 2025, this global initiative

insights.claim: FIT-P added five members in ten months — Malaysia and Paraguay in November, and South Korea, Peru and Thailand at the Auckland meeting — with Samoa and Fiji attending as observers and delegates from 21 countries participating.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: South Korea and Thailand joining moves FIT-P from a niche club toward a bloc with real Asian manufacturing weight — watch for further ASEAN accessions.
insights.locator: In the course of just ten months, five new members have joined

insights.claim: FIT-P members collectively account for close to 20% of global goods trade despite the group's modest individual economic heft.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: A fifth of goods trade is enough to set de facto standards on supply-chain rules even without any large-economy member.
insights.quote: this new group, representing close to 20% of global goods trade, is championing open and fair trade at a time when others are retreating
insights.locator: Its economic heft may not be giant

insights.claim: FIT-P's agenda is collaboration on strengthening supply chains, removing non-tariff barriers, integrating new technologies and facilitating investment — not conventional tariff liberalization.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Signals the emerging template for post-WTO trade deals: regulatory and supply-chain cooperation replaces market-access bargaining.
insights.locator: This innovative trade arrangement, where members agree

insights.claim: FIT-P membership reflects trade diversification as a pillar of economic security strategies rather than a move away from the United States, China or the EU.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Do not read minilateral bloc formation as decoupling — it is hedging, and it raises the option value of mid-sized trade partners.
insights.quote: having all your eggs in one or two baskets is not the best strategy for sustained economic growth
insights.locator: It doesn’t mean that these countries are necessarily moving away
